podcast.title: Arrest and Imprisonment (1998)
podcast.body: Following the British Airways incident, Ian Brown was arrested and, despite his testimony, a judge with alleged ties to the airline industry rejected his explanations and sentenced him to a four-month term in Strangeways prison in Manchester. His appeal, arguing that his UK tour would be canceled and over 100 people would lose work, was denied, with the judge aiming to "set an example." He was ultimately released unharmed before Christmas of that year. "The message to the public, he said, must be that anyone who behaves in this way will lose their liberty."

podcast.title: British Airways Air Rage and Imprisonment (1998)
podcast.body: On February 13, 1998, following an MTV event in Paris, Ian Brown boarded British Airways flight 1611 from Charles de Gaulle to Manchester. Once airborne, he reportedly argued with a flight attendant, allegedly threatening to cut her hands off, and then caused a disturbance near the cockpit by banging on the door and swearing at the crew during the plane's descent. Upon landing, he was arrested and charged with endangering the safety of an aircraft. Despite his defense, a judge with ties to the airline industry sentenced him to four months in Strangeways Prison in Manchester to "set an example," and he is now permanently banned from flying British Airways. "The message to the public, he said, must be that anyone who behaves in this way will lose their liberty."

podcast.title: British Airways Flight Incident (1998)
podcast.body: On February 13, 1998, not long after releasing his first solo album and while estranged from The Stone Roses, Ian Brown boarded British Airways Flight 1611 from Charles de Gaulle Airport to Manchester after an MTV event in Paris. Once airborne, he allegedly got into a row with a flight attendant, threatening to "cut your hands off," and then caused a disturbance by banging on the cockpit door and swearing at the crew during the plane's descent. Upon landing, he was arrested and charged with endangering the safety of an aircraft in flight. "Officially, Ian got into a row with a flight attendant over something, allegedly saying, I'm going to cut your hands off."

podcast.title: Lifetime Flight Ban (1998)
podcast.body: As a consequence of his actions and conviction, Ian Brown was permanently banned from flying with British Airways. "Fortunately, he was honed unharmed for Christmas of that year, but unfortunately, he'll never be permitted to fly British airways again."

podcast.title: Spotty Solo Career
podcast.body: As the singer of The Stone Roses, Ian Brown's solo career has been described as "extremely spotty," and certainly nothing close to the level of success or impact achieved by The Stone Roses in the early 1990s. "Both have had extremely spotty solo careers, and certainly nothing approaching what the roses were in the early 1990s."

xref.title: British Airways Air Rage Conviction (February 13, 1998) – Sentenced to Four Months in Strangeways
xref.body: Ian Brown boarded British Airways Flight 1611 from Paris to Manchester on February 13, 1998. During the short flight, a dispute arose with flight attendant Christine Cooper when she made what Brown interpreted as a dismissive wave. Brown allegedly shouted at her and threatened to chop off her hands; when the pilot came out to investigate, Brown reportedly repeated the threat. He was also said to have banged on the cockpit door for 20 to 30 seconds during descent. When the plane landed, he was arrested and charged with air rage. At trial in October 1998, Brown's defense — that his remarks were jokes and he never banged on the door — was not believed. On October 23, 1998, he was sentenced to four months at Strangeways prison. Brown maintained he was made an example because of a timing coincidence with a genuine air rage case in Spain, and claimed racism as a factor. "Ian and his friends and supporters maintained that he was set up as an example."

xref.title: Andy Rourke Death (May 18, 2023) – Pancreatic Cancer, Age 59; Sued Morrissey, Later Played Two Morrissey Singles
xref.body: Andy Rourke was a founding member of the Smiths and is considered by fans one of the greatest bassists in the history of British indie rock. His time with the band ended badly: a heroin addiction, a lawsuit against Morrissey and Johnny Marr for unpaid royalties (he was broke), and a decade later a bankruptcy over tax issues. Post-Smiths, he worked with the Pretenders, Killing Joke, Stone Roses singer Ian Brown, Dolores O'Riordan and the Cranberries, and Peter Hook of New Order. In a remarkable reconciliation, he played on two Morrissey solo singles despite the money disputes. His father and sister were both diagnosed with cancer, which prompted him to start a cancer charity; he himself was later diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. He died in a New York hospital on May 18, 2023, age 59. "Ask any Smiths fan, and they'll tell you that he was one of the greatest bassists in the history of British Indie Rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Claims of Being Set Up
xref.body: To this day, Ian Brown, along with his friends and supporters, maintains that he was unfairly targeted and set up as an example, asserting that he did not deserve to be sent to jail for the air rage incident. "To this day though, Ian and his friends and supporters maintained that he was set up as some kind of example and did not deserve to be sent to jail."

xref.title: Ian Brown's Air Rage Conviction
xref.body: On February 13, 1998, Ian Brown, the then-ex-lead singer of The Stone Roses, was arrested for "air rage" aboard British Airways Flight 1611 from Paris to Manchester. A flight attendant, Christine Cooper, alleged that after a misunderstanding, Brown yelled threats, including that he'd "chop her hands off," and later banged on the cockpit door for 20-30 seconds during the plane's descent. Brown denied the allegations in court, claiming his remarks were jokes and he didn't bang on the door, but was sentenced to four months in the notorious Strangeways Prison. "Ian was sentenced to four months in prison at the notorious Strangeways Prison."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Prison Experience at Strangeways
xref.body: While serving his four-month sentence at Strangeways Prison, a facility housing 1100 hardcore prisoners, Ian Brown adapted to the conditions. He joked about "turning Muslim" to avoid the "horrible meat pies" and get halal food like lentils, rice, and chicken. Despite guards allegedly trying to turn other prisoners against him, he was popular, giving autographs in exchange for cigarettes and newspapers. Authorities had to frequently move him due to his popularity. He read extensively and maintained physical fitness, doing 500 sit-ups and 400 push-ups daily, emerging in better shape than ever before. "He joked that he, quote, turned Muslim to avoid eating the horrible meat pies they served."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Solo Efforts Inferior to Band Output
xref.body: The individual solo careers of singer Ian Brown and guitarist John Squire were significantly less successful and impactful than the band's collective achievements, especially those from the early 1990s. This illustrates a case where "the whole is actually greater than the sum of its parts." "But when you split up singer Ian Brown and guitarist John Squire, again, not so much."
